greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who entrusts us to the care of His holy angels, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to the humility of a child: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you send your angels to watch over us: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you guide our steps along the everlasting way: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
homily:
We often imagine the spiritual life as a vast, complex architecture—a structure we must build with our own hands, brick by brick, through logic, effort, and careful planning. We look at the world, at its intricate systems and its vast horizons, and we feel like architects trying to map out a path that makes sense. We try to understand the 'why' of the universe, the 'how' of our own story, and the 'where' of our ultimate destination. But today, the Church invites us to stop building and start looking. Today, on the Memorial of the Holy Guardian Angels, the horizon of our faith shrinks, not to make it smaller, but to make it intimate. It shrinks to the size of a single, steady gaze.

Look at Job in our first reading. He is a man who has been brought to the very edge of his own understanding. He has seen the storm, he has felt the weight of the unknown, and he has realized that he is not the one who commands the morning or sets the boundaries of the sea. He stands before the Creator and finally says, 'Behold, I am of little account; what can I answer you? I put my hand over my mouth.' There is a profound, quiet strength in that silence. Job isn't giving up; he is letting go. He is admitting that he is not the author of the story, but a character held within it. He is realizing that the One who knit the earth together is the same One who is watching over him in the middle of the storm.

I want you to think about how Benjamin Vo lived his life. He was a boy of such brilliant, focused curiosity. He was the kind of person who looked at a system—whether it was the logic of a line of code or the complex flight path of a Boeing 737—and he didn't just see the mechanics. He saw the potential. He saw the beauty of how things were meant to work. He lived with a spirit that was always looking for the next horizon, always ready to ascend. And he did it with such a gentle, steady heart. He was a boy who understood that the world was a place of exploration, a place to be understood and loved. Think of the way he would talk about his dream of 'con chim airlines.' There was a giggle, a spark in his eye, a pure, unadulterated joy in the very idea of flight. That wasn't just a hobby; that was the reflection of a soul that was meant for the heights, a soul that knew, in its own way, that there was something more to life than the ground beneath our feet.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these past three months, the world has felt like it has lost its map. You remember the way Ben would come down the stairs, always the first to say, 'Good morning, Dad.' You remember the way he would listen to your stories, Alan, with such rapt attention, as if they were the most important things in the world. You remember the quiet joy of a family trip, the way you all moved through the world together. To look at the empty chair at the table feels like a betrayal of that bond. But please hear this: the Gospel today tells us that we are never truly alone. Jesus says, 'See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I say to you that their angels in heaven always look upon the face of my heavenly Father.'

Think about that. The angels are not just distant protectors. They are witnesses. They are the ones who are constantly looking at the face of the Father, and in that gaze, they see us, too. They see your sorrow, they see your love, they see the way you hold onto each other, and they see Benjamin. He is not lost to you. He is in the light of that same Face. The angels are the bridge between your home and the home where he now rests. When you feel a sudden, warm memory of his smile, that is a grace. When you see a bird in flight—that creature he loved so much—and it reminds you of his dream of 'con chim airlines,' that is a messenger. When you gather as a family, even when the table feels incomplete, the very fact that you are still loving each other, still holding on, is a sign that the angels are at work in your home.

Ryan, you are the one who carries that peace now. You are the brother who knows the rhythm of Ben’s heart. You know the secrets of the games he coded, the joy he found in the simple things, the way he looked at the world with wonder. When you walk into a room, you are carrying that legacy. You are carrying the curiosity, the kindness, and the love that you and Ben shared. You are not a brother who is walking alone. You are a brother who is walking with the strength of a love that has already arrived at the destination. Keep being the boy who is curious. Keep being the brother who knows that love is the only thing that actually lasts. You are a family of four, and that will never change. You are just living in two different rooms of the same house, and the door between them is held open by the grace of Christ.

There is a temptation, when we are grieving, to think that we have been left behind in the dark. We feel the absence of the smile, the silence of the morning greeting, the empty chair at the table. But the Gospel today gives us a different perspective. Jesus calls a child into the midst of the disciples. He doesn't say, 'Go and be great.' He says, 'Turn and become like children.' He invites us into the simplicity of trust. He invites us to be like Benjamin—a boy who could offer his entire piggy bank to help an uncle in need, not because he was calculating the cost, but because his heart was naturally oriented toward love. That offer was a prayer. It was a sign of a heart that was already aligned with the heart of Jesus. It wasn't about the money; it was about the heart that wanted to give everything it had. That is the kind of heart that enters the Kingdom.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that sometimes visits you in the quiet of the night. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of 'what if' or 'did I miss something.' I want to lift that stone from you today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what you are doing. You are taking the love that was poured into Ben, and you are letting it flow into the lives of others. You are ensuring that his life is not a closed chapter, but a living, breathing, life-sustaining force. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to forgive, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

We are on this earth, as the Psalm says, to see the bounty of the Lord in the land of the living. Sometimes that land feels like a desert. Sometimes it feels like we are waiting for a harvest that will never come. But the Gospel tells us that we are watched over. We are guarded. We are guided. We are never out of the sight of the Father. When the days feel long and the silence feels heavy, remember that you are not being asked to understand the mysteries of the universe. You are being asked to trust the One who holds the stars in place and who holds Benjamin in the palm of His hand. You are being asked to live in such a way that his memory continues to be a blessing to everyone you meet.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His holy angels guide you along the everlasting way. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
petition_call: For these prayers, we pray to the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all families who carry the weight of grief, that God may console them with His presence and fill them with the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
The LORD addressed Job out of the storm and said:Have you ever in your lifetime commanded the morning
and shown the dawn its place
For taking hold of the ends of the earth,
till the wicked are shaken from its surface?
The earth is changed as is clay by the seal,
and dyed as though it were a garment;
But from the wicked the light is withheld,
and the arm of pride is shattered.Have you entered into the sources of the sea,
or walked about in the depths of the abyss?
Have the gates of death been shown to you,
or have you seen the gates of darkness?
Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth?
Tell me, if you know all:
Which is the way to the dwelling place of light,
and where is the abode of darkness,
That you may take them to their boundaries
and set them on their homeward paths?
You know, because you were born before them,
and the number of your years is great!Then Job answered the LORD and said:Behold, I am of little account; what can I answer you?
I put my hand over my mouth.
Though I have spoken once, I will not do so again;
though twice, I will do so no more.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (24b) Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
O LORD, you have probed me and you know me;
you know when I sit and when I stand;
you understand my thoughts from afar.
My journeys and my rest you scrutinize,
with all my ways you are familiar.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
Where can I go from your spirit?
From your presence where can I flee?
If I go up to the heavens, you are there;
if I sink to the nether world, you are present there.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
If I take the wings of the dawn,
if I settle at the farthest limits of the sea,
Even there your hand shall guide me,
and your right hand hold me fast.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
Truly you have formed my inmost being;
you knit me in my mother’s womb.
I give you thanks that I am fearfully, wonderfully made; 
wonderful are your works.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
The disciples approached Jesus and said,
“Who is the greatest in the Kingdom of heaven?”
He called a child over, placed it in their midst, and said,
“Amen, I say to you, unless you turn and become like children,
you will not enter the Kingdom of heaven.
Whoever humbles himself like this child
is the greatest in the Kingdom of heaven.
And whoever receives one child such as this in my name receives me.“See that you do not despise one of these little ones,
for I say to you that their angels in heaven
always look upon the face of my heavenly Father.”

day: Memorial of the Holy Guardian Angels

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.
